competitive_landscape: The cluster is served today by a distributed set of dive-resort and speedboat operators (Murex, Eco Divers, Lembeh Resort, Bastianos and others) running diesel craft on short transfers, plus state ferries to the outer islands. The pain is noisy, wake-heavy, fume-emitting boats operating inside a marine biosphere, and slow, exposed runs to the outer archipelago. Demand is real and recovering fast; the experience is exactly the diesel status quo a clean fleet improves on.

journeys.today: A 30–40 minute diesel speedboat ride, noisy and wake-heavy, straight through a UNESCO biosphere reef.
journeys.with_navier: A quiet, near-silent foiling hop of ~8–12 nm with zero local emissions, dropping foil for the shallow reef approach to the resort jetties.

journeys.today: A long road transfer to Bitung then a boat across, or a slow open-water run around the peninsula tip.
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~30 nm foiling passage to the muck-diving capital, replacing the road-plus-boat slog with one smooth crossing.

journeys.today: An overnight inter-island ferry or a long, exposed small-craft run to the remote northern volcanic islands.
journeys.with_navier: A long-range hybrid passage that reaches the frontier archipelago in a single comfortable run, refuelling on diesel with no charging infrastructure needed up north.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire core cluster is in all-electric range: Manado↔Bunaken (~8–12 nm), Likupang↔Bangka (~25–30 nm) and Manado↔Lembeh (~30 nm by sea) all sit inside the 70 nm envelope, and the greenfield SEZ piers can be designed for charging from the start. This is the platform for the high-frequency dive-and-resort transfers that carry the volume.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for the outer-island line-haul: Manado↔Sangihe (~140 nm) and the remote Talaud chain exceed all-electric range and suit the long-range hybrid, which refuels on diesel and needs no charging at the frontier islands. Keep the core reef cluster and the outer-island line as separate networks, not one continuous chain.

precedents.what: ~100-vessel, $100M phased clean-marine network with JIH Global, first 5 vessels in 2026
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves a clean-marine network financed and built across a dive/resort archipelago — directly transferable to a super-priority marine destination with a new pier programme.

regulatory_note: Bunaken National Park is managed under the forestry/conservation authority (KLHK, distinct from the fisheries marine-protected-area regime elsewhere in Sulawesi), giving a clean, low-wake, quiet-mode fleet a direct conservation rationale — sharpened by the park's 40th MAB anniversary in 2026. The greenfield Likupang SEZ runs through the state economic-zone developer, opening a clean route to spec charging and clean-fleet operation into new piers.
seasonality: North-facing onto the Celebes/Sulawesi Sea, the cluster sees its roughest water during the northwest monsoon and Pacific-fringe swell (Dec–Mar), with the calmest dive conditions May–Oct. The reef transfers are short and largely sheltered; foiling holds a smooth ride through the short monsoon chop that disrupts diesel day-boats, and the outer-island runs benefit most from the long-range hybrid's sea-keeping.

summary: Likupang is a federal super-priority destination and special economic zone at the tip of North Sulawesi, anchored on Manado and opening onto Bunaken National Marine Park, the legendary muck-diving of Lembeh Strait, and Bangka Island. Divers and resort guests reach these reefs today on diesel speedboats — 30–40 minutes from Manado, run straight through one of the oldest marine biosphere reserves on earth. The cluster's working routes are short and sheltered (7–35 nm), foreign arrivals are surging through Manado's airport, and a greenfield resort SEZ is being built with new piers right now: a clean, fast foiling fleet fits the geography, the conservation mandate, and the build window all at once.
tagline: Gateway to one of the world's great dive coasts — every reef reached today by diesel day-boat through a protected park.

use_cases.body: Replace diesel speedboats on the Manado↔Bunaken and Likupang↔Bangka transfers with quiet, wake-light all-electric foiling — faster, smoother and zero-emission through a protected marine park, a tangible upgrade for the dive-resort cluster.
use_cases.title: Clean dive-and-resort transfers
